catalog_quote: 4.3 Tekanan pada Suku Kata Pola /KV/. Tekanan suku kata pada bahasa Iha, secara umum, jika tidak dapat ditentukan, terutama pada kata yang bersuku tiga, maka suku kata kedua (tengah) cenderung mendapat tekanan. Kondisi yang lain adalah apabila sebuah kata terbentuk dari unsur perulangan, maka suku kata pertama dari bentuk perulangan itulah yang dikenai tekanan. Meskipun dinyatakan demikian, sekali lagi hal ini tidak mutlak. Untuk memperoleh gambaran tentang tekanan dalam bahasa Iha, berikut ini diberikan bebarapa contoh kata yang berpola /KV/ sebagai berikut: /'ne/ 'nama' 192 /'me.re/ 'dalam' 21 /ma.'nda/ 'anak' 203 /wi.'ri.da/ 'kencing' 70 /ha.'pa.ra.ta/ 'tempurung, batok' 5 (312) /to.hi.'to.hi/ 'cawat' 382 /tom.'tom.ndi/ 'patung' 235 ... 5.4.1 Tekanan. new_statements.quote: Tekanan suku kata pada bahasa Iha, secara umum, jika tidak dapat ditentukan, terutama pada kata yang bersuku tiga, maka suku kata kedua (tengah) cenderung mendapat tekanan. Kondisi yang lain adalah apabila sebuah kata terbentuk dari unsur perulangan, maka suku kata pertama dari bentuk perulangan itulah yang dikenai tekanan. Meskipun dinyatakan demikian, sekali lagi hal ini tidak mutlak. [...] Tekanan dalam bahasa Iha, meskipun tidak mengandung fungsi fonemis, tidak begitu saja terlupakan. Tekanan dalam bahasa Iha tidak dapat diramalkan sebelumnya. Pengaruh perbedaan fonetis (bukan fonemis) yang menonjol adalah bahwa vokal pada tempat tekanan cenderung mengalami alternasi panjang.
new_statements.translation: Syllable stress in Iha, in general, when it cannot be determined, especially in three-syllable words, the second (middle) syllable tends to receive stress. Another condition is that when a word is formed from a reduplicated element, it is the first syllable of the reduplicated form that bears the stress. Although it is stated thus, once again this is not absolute. [...] Stress in Iha, although it carries no phonemic function, is not simply to be overlooked. Stress in Iha cannot be predicted in advance. The salient phonetic (not phonemic) effect is that the vowel in the stressed position tends to undergo an alternation in length.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive but its position is described as not predictable; the only tendency given is that in words of three or more syllables the second syllable is stressed (examples /wi.'ri.da/ 'urinate', /ha.'pa.ra.ta/ 'coconut shell'), while the disyllabic examples vary between initial (/'me.re/ 'inside') and final (/ma.'nda/ 'child'). The stressed vowel is phonetically lengthened (['ko:gri] 'lungs', [me'he:q] 'neck', ['pu:har] 'navel').
new_statements.exceptions: Reduplicated words: stress on the first syllable of the reduplicated form; the authors add that the tendencies are 'not absolute' (tidak mutlak). Variable placement in disyllables ('me.re vs ma.'nda).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms from the authors' wordlist (numbers after each example are wordlist entry numbers). Stress is explicitly non-phonemic. Note: later work reported second-hand in Cottet 2015:100-101 (Donohue 2005:48; Donohue & Gregory 2014) treats Iha/West Bomberai as having a pitch accent system and hypothesises contrastive grammatical tones carried by suffixes with minimal functional load; and the stress-marked transcriptions from Walker & Himmelmann's unpublished 2022 description quoted in Al-Gariri 2022 consistently show final stress in disyllables ([mbɛˈd̪ɛn], pɛhɛ́r, kɔmbɔ́r, kondón). The 1992 statement may therefore be superseded once Walker & Himmelmann's description appears.
new_statements.identity_note: Iha (ihp; older name Kapaur; Dutch 'Ihandin') of the Fakfak/Onin area. Flassy & Animung 1992 describe Iha as a whole with no dialect named. The Walker & Himmelmann / Al-Gariri data come from one adult male speaker in the DoBeS Iha corpus (Narfafan & Tuturop 2009). Cottet 2015 describes the sister language Mbahám (baha1259), not Iha; its Iha remarks are second-hand from Donohue.

sources.note: Section 1.2 gives only the consonant and vowel inventories (after Walker & Himmelmann 2022:2-3); no statement on stress placement. Transcriptions taken from Walker & Himmelmann's dictionary mark stress on the final syllable of disyllables: [mbɛˈd̪ɛn] ~ mbɛdɛ́n 'season', pɛhɛ́r 'sea water', kɔmbɔ́r, kondón, qpawɔ́- (pp. 4, 12ff. and appendix tables). The 'High/Non-' column in the data tables is following-vowel height, not tone. Data: one adult male speaker from the DoBeS Iha corpus (Narfafan & Tuturop 2009).

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Sister language (Mbahám). On Iha it reports second-hand (pp. 100-101): 'In Iha, the closest related language to Mbahám, Donohue & Gregory (2014) hypothesize the existence of contrastive tones carried by suffixes and realized on the stem. The functional load of these tones is minimal. According to Donohue (2005:48), not only Iha but also Mbahám and Karas, i.e. the whole West Bomberai group, have a pitch accent system..'. Cottet herself treats Mbahám as a stress language with unexplained F0 movements.
